note: N-104 / R30 route A. ECDemo.checkMulIdentity() computes ecMul(this.pt, 1n), which the always-on EC optimizer rewrites to this.pt (ec-mul-one). The rewrite used to drop the operand validation ecMul performs first (R-157: on the curve, or exactly O), so a deployer-supplied off-curve or non-canonical pt made checkMulIdentity() SUCCEED with the optimizer on and ABORT with it off: one source, two meanings. The rewrite now keeps that gate (assert(pt === O || ecOnCurve(pt))) ahead of the alias, in all seven tiers, which is what moved this fixture's golden. Every spend below executes the fixture's actual compiled locking script on @bsv/sdk Spend. The two 'attack' rejects are the forced near-misses: both were ACCEPTED by the pre-fix compiler (measured, remediation-logs/N-104/witness-prefix.txt) and are rejected now, exactly as the unoptimized ecMul rejects them. The O accept pins that O is exempt from the gate, as it is inside ecMul.
